newsitem.title: USA: Fire aboard Cunard cruise liner extinguished.
newsitem.headline: Fire aboard Cunard cruise liner extinguished.

text.p: Fire broke out in a linen locker aboard a cruise ship near the Bahamas on Sunday, forcing hundreds of passengers to prepare to abandon ship as crew members fought the blaze, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The fire aboard the 627-foot (190-meter) Cunard liner Vista Fjord was extinguished after the ship pulled into port at Freeport, Bahamas, more than three hours after the crew radioed for help, a Coast Guard spokesman said. None of the 991 passengers and crew was hurt.

The ship put out a distress call from about 20 miles (32 km) south of Freeport, Bahamas, at 1:40 a.m. (0640 GMT), a few hours after its departure from Miami Saturday night enroute to Funchol on the Portuguese island of Madeir, the Coast Guard said.

As its crew fought the fire and headed the ship toward Freeport, the Coast Guard dispatched a boat and a plane to help and three other cruise ships, the Veendam, Destiny and Leeward, diverted in case passengers had to abandon ship, Coast Guard Petty Officer David French said.
The Vista Fjord arrived at Freeport about 5:20 a.m. (0920 GMT) and the crew, with help from Bahamian firefighters, extinguished the blaze within an hour, French said.
